title: Workspace hub
goal: Open the workspace and be one press away from where the work is.
_why: Every one of the five areas is a DESTINATION: nothing here is read, compared or processed, so the task is navigate and R9 chooses tiles. The tempting wrong answer is a table with a count column — fully conformant, and wrong twice: rows invite comparing five numbers nobody compares, and a destination rendered as a row stops looking enterable. The moment this screen grows content of its own (a feed, a summary), the archetype flips to overview and this spec is wrong out loud.

zones.name: header
zones.purpose: The workspace's name and nothing else: no actions, because nothing is created from the hub — each area owns its own creations. No count Badge beside the title either; the counts belong to the tiles they describe.

zones.name: areas
zones.purpose: One tile per area, all five always present — they are the workspace's shape, not its content, so this grid never has an empty case of its own. Each tile is one target (Card interactive): the area's name, the one line saying what waits inside, and the live count riding the tile as a CountBadge — on the tile because the number describes the destination, never a column, because a column is an invitation to compare five numbers nobody compares (R9: entry points are tiles).

states.empty: EmptyState with icon=folder only if a workspace ever arrives with no areas provisioned (a half-created client) — saying the workspace is still being set up. Deliberately unreachable today: the five areas are fixed, and the spec records the state so the day provisioning becomes real the screen already knows what to say.
states.error: Counts that cannot be read render the tiles without their CountBadge rather than blocking the hub: the doors still work when the numbers do not, and a Badge tone=warning beside the failing area's title says its count is unavailable.

acceptance: Each area is exactly one press: the whole tile is the target, not a link inside it.
No area's count renders as a table column or a count strip — the number rides its own tile.
All five areas are visible without scrolling at desktop widths.
Nothing on the screen sorts, filters or searches the areas.

behaviours.given: the hub with its five areas
behaviours.when: the consultant presses anywhere on the documents tile
behaviours.then: the documents area opens — no inner link needed, the tile is the door
behaviours.why: The screen exists to be left through the right door (brief, verbatim).
behaviours.pendingReason: Delivered as a single screen file ahead of the product's own repo and test harness; the test lands with the first vitest setup, named workspace-hub#tile-opens-area.

data: areas: name, whatWaits (one line), count — five fixed areas (documents, meetings, decisions, people, reports) inline in the screen; opening records the chosen area in local state so the navigation is real
openQuestions: Whether the hub ever gains recent activity per area (last edited document, next meeting). That is the overview archetype's territory and would retire this spec, not extend it.
